text: Are curious about how to model the Wi-Fi MAC. You can look at this paper, and of course it exploits this modeling approach based on queues and servers. This this approach has been studied by many people. If you are again interested in queueing models for networks, Kleinrock is Kleinrock is the one who developed this queueing theory for networking. He is a professor at UCLA in California, US, and he has wrote two books about how to model networks using queueing models. And there are many different variants of queueing models that have been developed, just to say. So this is just as complementary information. Anyway, that said, let's consider our Wi-Fi network and let's start by describing how our MAC layer works. Now, as I said, in Wi-Fi, the MAC layer is the function that decides when and how to serve a packet. Right, a packet.
